newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks fall sharply to close down.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks fall sharply to close down.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks fell sharply just before the close on Tuesday on pre-U.S. election jitters and profit-taking from both local and overseas institutions, brokers said.
"The market's fall was a bit of a surprise after the strength in the morning and must be short-term traders locking in profits ahead of the election," said a broker with a large European house.
The Hang Seng Index dropped 56.70 points in the last 15 minutes of trading to close at 12,502.70. It hit an intraday high of 12,616.37 mid-morning.
Turnover was a bullish HK$7.48 billion, higher than Monday's HK$6.34 billion.
"The chief worry is that we will see another serious imbalance in the U.S. Congress, said Kieren Hung, sales director at G.K. Goh.
Brokers said the Hang Seng Index futures market was not very active. A total of 10,194 contracts were traded with open interest remaining fairly steady at 41,372 contracts.
The November contract shed 40 points to close at 12,485, a 17 point discount to the cash market.
Brokers said there was little talk of market risk associated with holding open positions while Russia President Boris Yeltsin underwent heart surgery.
Among the blue chips, utilities were the worst performing. The commercial and industrial sector was the only sector which managed a modest gain.

Hongkong Telecom dropped HK$0.25 to HK$13.35. The company released its first half results for 1997 showing a 12.1 percent increase in net profit. Brokers said the results were in line with expectations.

China Light sank HK$0.60 to HK$35.50 on healthy turnover of HK$192.15 million after reporting a 14.8 percent fall in profits for the year ended September 30. The company warned sales growth for the remainder of the decade would be low.

Property stocks were bid up until the last 15 minutes of trade, buoyed intitally by the government's report on Monday on October property sales, but fell in line with the rest of the market. The October sales figures showed the number of average monthly property sales in 1996 exceeded the monthly average in 1993, a boom year. Cheung Kong put on HK$0.50 to HK$62.50.
